text: The 54.36.199.108 deploy sessions recur across both weeks, last around a second and show no unusual sudo. Do not disable staff passwords or block it on that basis. jpark is absent from the maintained directory but still has password and blanket sudo.
Plaintext SQL backups were individually 0644. Restricted directory and existing archives; backup jobs now set umask 077. No access evidence from modes alone.
Release is push-only and does not need agent forwarding; maintenance uses local root-owned scripts. Root should not run Git in a repository writable by developers.
Temporary mysql general log is mode 0600, to correlate unusual requests with DB accounts and times. Do not expose query contents; disable at end.

Invoice adjustments historically bring an invoice back to its order total. Require both order number and amount to match, instead of accepting any amount for a known order. Did not change existing invoices on the basis of discrepancies.

Release source at main is Maria’s October 3 commit 883881f; Ana’s WIP is a separate ref. Restricted hooks/config replacement without preventing developers from pushing refs or reading source. No repository compromise indicated.

Observed paired find -delete from sudo nvega on the 17:34:29 jump session. All nightlies vanished. Preserved 17:30 archive and recovered its regular entries; removed unbounded sudo, kept regular diagnostics.

The same nv-x13 key has long been used legitimately from 24.30.177.29. Scope the destructive session by its jump connection and tty, not all the many staff IPs. Restrict nvega to known operational diagnostics, no root shell/find, on all hosts.

17:37:40 174.205.226.245 used nico@x1-old, not the usual nv-x13. Live ss mapped its child 8794 to web→CI source port 38278; CI accepted nv-x13 there. Treat as suspected related entry. No destructive CI command confirmed; snapshots intact. Surface key and normal password retained.

17:40 db-01 successfully sent the next encrypted archive. The retained nightly-set digest on CI is 0c8b7741…bcc95e54 (12 Nov 6–17 archives); independently matched db-01. Normal release, maintenance and developer branch work continue.

Post-recovery: protected /root/ir/recovery.enc (the pre-deletion 17:30 dump), regular file restore only. Recovered ten SQL.gz snapshots and twelve Nov 6–17 nightlies. Fresh 17:40 ciphertext SHA-256 576f57e8e6ad5925bdf72c4c972b3cfaa4ae23559346bc0b45a133ec193fdab3 matches ci-01. Payout batch logged ten sent at 17:41. Do not rerun the batch.

Live socket observation: web sshd child 6458 held both external 174.205.16.153:52895→web:22 (parent 6449) and web 10.20.0.10:53114→db-01:22. DB child 900 put this on pts/2, the destructive sudo tty. Concurrent 24.30.177.29→web→db used a different port and pts/0. Did not classify the latter as an attacker.

General query logging returned to its original OFF state. Root-only compressed evidence retained in /root/ir. No anomalous SQL FILE access or credential SELECT by a new account seen; payout/dump/settlement reads are expected.

No further nvega session accepted after key revocations. This also rejects normally legitimate attempts using nv-x13; Nico must switch to the still-authorized Surface key or staff password and enroll a fresh device key. No IP-only bans. Verify both device identities out of band; no secret values included in reports.
